statusDetail: Coverage complete across six representative public templates. Checkout after purchase, authenticated test execution, and account cancellation were not covered because they require credentials/payment.

page.framework: Angular SSR on core site; WordPress blog
page.notes: Large public exam-preparation and subscription service. The remote target is unrelated to the repo playground config, so that scoped config was not applied.

checkOutcomes.method: Emulated prefers-color-scheme: dark and compared screenshot/computed CSS.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The dark-condition screenshot is visually identical to light; computed color-scheme is normal and CSS probe found no dark preference rule.

checkOutcomes.method: Emulated prefers-reduced-motion: reduce and inspected document animations.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Three animations remained running under reduce (durations 1000, 1000, and 2500 ms), and no reduced-motion CSS rule was found.

checkOutcomes.method: Inspected contrast preference CSS and Lighthouse contrast audit.
checkOutcomes.evidence: No prefers-contrast or forced-colors styling was found; Lighthouse found 31 color-contrast failures.

checkOutcomes.method: Inspected CSS and representative route/state changes.
checkOutcomes.evidence: No View Transition CSS/API use was found across the Angular homepage and representative navigation surfaces; state changes are abrupt.

checkOutcomes.method: Inspected CSS for scroll timelines and observed scrolling during layout and heap interaction captures.
checkOutcomes.evidence: No scroll-linked storytelling/parallax behavior or JavaScript-driven scroll animation was observed, so the page avoids the main-thread anti-pattern.

checkOutcomes.method: Exercised mobile scrolling and inspected representative controls.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Native scrolling and ordinary tap controls worked without custom gesture interception or scroll fighting on audited mobile paths.

checkOutcomes.method: Reviewed desktop/mobile screenshots and long-page scrolling.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Navigation adapts between desktop header and mobile menu while long content remains scrollable; no blocking fixed chrome was observed.

checkOutcomes.method: Inspected overlay/menu CSS and edge behavior.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The site has dropdown/menu and floating notification UI, but no CSS anchor positioning or fallback-position rules were found.

checkOutcomes.method: Reviewed hierarchy and navigation cues on homepage, exam detail, listing, and Pass page.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Headings, selected Pass navigation, direct CTA labels, and content grouping provide visible orientation on representative routes.

checkOutcomes.method: Captured first viewport on desktop and mobile before interaction.
checkOutcomes.evidence: A fixed notification-permission banner occupies the bottom of both first viewports while promotional chrome and WhatsApp also compete with core content.

checkOutcomes.method: Inspected DOM and computed styles for overlays.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The persistent notification UI is custom chrome rather than a native dialog/popover flow; the DOM reports a role=dialog surface and no popover primitive.

checkOutcomes.method: Compared content/chrome balance in first-viewport screenshots.
checkOutcomes.evidence: On mobile, the trial banner, fixed notification prompt, WhatsApp control, header, and app badges crowd the primary preparation content.

checkOutcomes.method: Ran layout primitive at 360x800 across five templates.

checkOutcomes.method: Inspected CSS and compared reused components across desktop/mobile.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The CSS probe found no container queries; reusable cards/navigation rely on viewport-wide treatment and the listing overflows at 360 px.

checkOutcomes.method: Focused visible controls, read outlines and measured target boxes.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Several focused links report outline:none and many exam-category controls are only 34 px tall, below a comfortable touch target.

checkOutcomes.method: Reviewed first viewports and heading/CTA labels across core paths.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The homepage states “Complete Exam Preparation” with Get Started For Free; listing, exam detail, signup, and Pass routes expose clear next actions.

checkOutcomes.method: Visually reviewed typography across desktop and mobile screenshots.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Core headings and body text reflow without clipping on sampled home, signup, Pass, blog, and detail views.

checkOutcomes.method: Checked viewport/reflow via layout and measured interactive targets.

checkOutcomes.method: Ran Lighthouse errors-in-console audit.

checkOutcomes.method: Inspected doctype/charset and ran Lighthouse plus image audit.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Doctype and UTF-8 are valid, but Lighthouse found four aspect-ratio failures and image inspection found 54 images without explicit dimensions.

checkOutcomes.method: Reviewed Lighthouse best-practices and load behavior for prompts/errors.
checkOutcomes.evidence: No console exception or browser permission prompt occurred on load; notification consent is rendered as site UI with a defer option.

checkOutcomes.method: Inspected rendered/raw metadata and Lighthouse SEO.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Homepage and sampled content expose descriptive titles and meta descriptions; Lighthouse passed both audits.

checkOutcomes.method: Inspected anchors, viewport, robots, and Lighthouse SEO.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Viewport and robots are valid, but Lighthouse found 77 non-crawlable anchors; recon shows many javascript:void(0) links for categories and actions.

checkOutcomes.method: Fetched robots/sitemap and ran raw HTTP discoverability checks on representative templates.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Homepage/detail return 200 with canonical/sitemap signals, but the public blog index raw fetch returned HTTP 500 while still rendering content.

checkOutcomes.method: Inspected rendered DOM for JSON-LD and Open Graph metadata.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Homepage DOM contains application/ld+json and Open Graph title, description, URL, type, image, locale, and site metadata matching visible content.

checkOutcomes.method: Ran headers and cookies primitives.
checkOutcomes.evidence: HTTPS is used, but CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, and Permissions-Policy are absent; all 15 observed cookies were flagged insecure.

checkOutcomes.method: Ran HAR and tracker enumeration.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Load contacted 22 third-party origins and five known trackers; 70 third-party requests transferred 1.33 MB, including Google, Facebook, DoubleClick, Bing, and WebEngage.

checkOutcomes.method: Inspected signup flow and authentication affordances.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Signup uses a mobile-number/OTP entry with no visible passkey/WebAuthn option; phishing-resistant authentication was not offered on the sampled auth path.

checkOutcomes.method: Ran security-header and cookie policy primitives.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Only X-Frame-Options was present; HSTS, CSP/frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, and nosniff were absent, and many cookies use SameSite=None without Secure.

checkOutcomes.method: Compared raw HTML with rendered DOM and crawler screenshots.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Raw HTML preserves 98% of home and 100% of exam-detail content, including titles, h1, and descriptions; neither route is a JS shell.

checkOutcomes.method: Exercised mobile layouts, scrolling, menus/controls, and representative routes.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Core content remained rendered and scrollable across sampled mobile routes without blank shells or clipped primary content.

checkOutcomes.method: Inspected manifest/service-worker affordances and adverse-network suitability.
checkOutcomes.evidence: No manifest link was present in recon and no offline fallback was evidenced for this app-like exam-preparation service.

checkOutcomes.method: Fetched public blog route outside browser rendering and compared crawler/browser state.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The blog index returns HTTP 500 while rendering a normal content page, providing a misleading success-like UI and broken status signal rather than intentional recovery.

checkOutcomes.method: Inspected document language/direction and CSS logical-property use.
checkOutcomes.evidence: html lang=en is present, but no dir and no logical inline/block properties were detected despite the site exposing language switching and localized content.

checkOutcomes.method: Reviewed localized navigation and commercial rendering.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The interface exposes language selection and renders Indian currency/number conventions consistently on the sampled Pass and home surfaces.

checkOutcomes.method: Reviewed sampled routes for time-zone-sensitive scheduling interactions.
checkOutcomes.evidence: No user-entered scheduling or cross-time-zone event flow was present in the audited public routes.
checkOutcomes.reason: No representative time-zone-sensitive interaction exists on the selected public templates.

checkOutcomes.method: Reviewed trial, notification, signup, and pricing surfaces for deceptive defaults.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Notification can be deferred, trial close is visible, Pass pricing and renewal are disclosed, and no preselected add-on was observed.

checkOutcomes.method: Submitted signup with an empty required input and captured the result.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The blank mobile-number submission produced no visible required-field feedback or actionable error.

checkOutcomes.method: Inspected signup input semantics and autocomplete.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The mobile-number step is not represented by a semantic form in the rendered DOM and its input exposes no autocomplete token, reducing autofill/input assistance.

checkOutcomes.method: Reviewed Pass pricing and signup entry.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Pass shows annual price, crossed-out reference price, total, 365-day validity, renewal text, and a specific purchase CTA before commitment.

checkOutcomes.method: Ran images primitive and HAR weight analysis.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Of 98 images, 64 use legacy formats, 16 are oversized, 15 lack responsive sources, and 54 lack dimensions.

checkOutcomes.method: Ran trace, HAR, and tracker primitives over an idle load.
checkOutcomes.evidence: An idle homepage load executes 50 scripts, transfers 2.12 MB of script, and records 70 third-party requests plus 864.91 ms blocking time.

checkOutcomes.method: Measured third-party bytes and origin count in HAR.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Third parties account for 1.33 MB across 70 requests; duplicate Google tags and Facebook/WebEngage code consume substantial budget before user interaction.

checkOutcomes.method: Reviewed public site intent and rendered/source affordances.
checkOutcomes.evidence: No declared agent-facing intent was available for this public exam-preparation audit.
checkOutcomes.reason: Agent-facing tools and on-device inference are emerging opportunities, not required for the audited user journeys.

checkOutcomes.method: Reviewed public site intent and rendered/source affordances.
checkOutcomes.evidence: No declared agent-facing intent was available for this public exam-preparation audit.
checkOutcomes.reason: Agent-facing tools and on-device inference are emerging opportunities, not required for the audited user journeys.

checkOutcomes.method: Compared baseline heap with a post snapshot after ten full-page down/up scroll cycles.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Node count grew 924,210 to 933,764 and self size 54.76 MB to 55.69 MB (about 1.7%); this bounded change does not evidence unbounded retained growth.

checkOutcomes.method: Inspected heap summary totals against the large Angular/content page.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Post-interaction heap remained about 55.7 MB with 933,764 snapshot nodes, proportionate to the large rendered homepage and stable relative to baseline.

checkOutcomes.method: Compared heap summary totals before/after repeated scrolling.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The small 1.7% total-size delta after ten cycles did not show a runaway population; constructor-level detached-node evidence was not exposed by this compact summary, so confidence is low.

principleOutcomes.reason: Agent-facing tools and on-device inference are emerging opportunities, not required for the audited user journeys.

paths.description: Homepage and primary acquisition entry point; tested desktop, mobile, dark theme, reduced motion, crawlability, performance, privacy, accessibility, and memory.
SSC CGL exam detail, representing long-form exam/content templates and navigation into preparation.
Online test-series listing, representing browsable product/listing templates.
Signup entry flow, representing the primary account conversion form; blank submission exercised.
Testbook Pass pricing page, representing commercial offer and subscription disclosure.
Blog index, representing editorial content and WordPress template behavior.

findings.summary: Honours prefers-reduced-motion: non-essential animations and auto-advance are reduced or removed when the user asks for less motion.
findings.evidence: Three animations remained running under reduce (durations 1000, 1000, and 2500 ms), and no reduced-motion CSS rule was found.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a reduce media query that removes non-essential motion and auto-advance.

findings.summary: Honours prefers-contrast / forced-colors: controls, text and scrollbars remain visible under high-contrast preferences.
findings.evidence: No prefers-contrast or forced-colors styling was found; Lighthouse found 31 color-contrast failures.
findings.suggestedFix: Add forced-colors and prefers-contrast treatments and fix measured contrast failures.

findings.summary: No intrusive pop-ups, interstitials or banners that obscure content on load; overlays are dismissible and content-first.
findings.evidence: A fixed notification-permission banner occupies the bottom of both first viewports while promotional chrome and WhatsApp also compete with core content.
findings.suggestedFix: Defer notification promotion until user intent and remove fixed first-load obstruction.

findings.summary: Touch targets are adequately sized and hover-only affordances have a non-hover fallback, and keyboard focus is visible, so the UI works for touch, pointer and keyboard alike.
findings.evidence: Several focused links report outline:none and many exam-category controls are only 34 px tall, below a comfortable touch target.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide visible :focus-visible styling and at least 44px comfortable touch targets.

findings.summary: Loading, empty, success, error, offline, and partial-completion states are visible and actionable; users can retry, undo, cancel, go back, or continue without losing context.
findings.evidence: Blank submission left the page visually unchanged with no inline error, recovery instruction, or announced required-field state.
findings.suggestedFix: Show and announce a specific mobile-number required error after attempted submission.

findings.summary: Core Web Vitals are in the good range: LCP is fast, interaction latency (INP) is low, and CLS is minimal; work is prioritised and deferred sensibly.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 7.9 s, TBT 760 ms, and CLS 0.132; the trace measured LCP 7.13 s and 864.91 ms total blocking time.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the LCP element, reduce blocking scripts, and address layout shifts to reach good CWV.

findings.summary: No cumulative layout shift from late content (images, banners, fonts) that arrives without reserved space.
findings.evidence: Mobile layout observation measured CLS 0.183 on home and 0.169 on the exam detail; 54 of 98 images lack dimensions.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve dimensions/aspect-ratio for images and stop late animated banner shifts.

findings.summary: The main thread is not blocked by long tasks or heavy scripting; work is deferred, chunked, prioritised, or moved off-thread.
findings.evidence: Trace recorded six long tasks, a 667.58 ms longest task, and 864.91 ms total blocking time.
findings.suggestedFix: Defer and split analytics/application work; schedule non-critical tasks after interaction/idle.

findings.summary: Critical resources are delivered efficiently: cache headers are useful, render-blocking chains are short, fonts do not block or shift text, HTTP delivery is modern, and network dependency trees do not delay the main content.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 118 requests and 2.86 MB transferred; 50 scripts carried 2.12 MB and several parser-inserted high-priority scripts are candidates in the critical path.
findings.suggestedFix: Shorten the critical chain, defer non-critical scripts, and apply effective caching/preload priorities.

findings.summary: The page does not ship large unused or duplicated JavaScript/CSS, avoidable legacy bundles, or third-party code that dominates the load without user value.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 611 KiB unused JavaScript and 53 KiB unused CSS; multiple GTM/gtag and Facebook bundles dominate transfer.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove duplicate tag containers and ship route-level code/CSS only when needed.

findings.summary: Interactive elements have accessible names, correct roles, and form fields have labels; images have alt text where meaningful; canvas/expressive content is exposed to assistive technology.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found seven unnamed links and an image-alt failure; image inspection found four images without alt text.
findings.suggestedFix: Name every link/control and add meaningful alt text or empty alt for decoration.

findings.summary: Text and essential UI meet WCAG colour-contrast minimums against their background.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported 31 failing contrast nodes on the homepage.
findings.suggestedFix: Adjust text and control colors to meet WCAG contrast minimums.

findings.summary: Heading and landmark structure is logical, focus order follows reading order, keyboard focus is always visible, and interactive state survives DOM moves.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found three heading-order failures; the document has two h1 elements and no main landmark, while multiple focused controls suppress outlines.
findings.suggestedFix: Use one page h1, add main/landmarks, repair heading order, and preserve visible focus.

findings.summary: The experience remains usable when zoomed or reflowed, touch targets are large enough, media has captions or equivalents where needed, and the viewport does not prevent user scaling.
findings.evidence: Viewport scaling is allowed, but many controls are 34 px tall and the test-series template overflows by 8 px at 360 px.
findings.suggestedFix: Fix listing reflow and increase undersized targets without disabling zoom.

findings.summary: Links are crawlable (real href), there is a viewport meta tag, robots does not block indexing, and link text is descriptive.
findings.evidence: Viewport and robots are valid, but Lighthouse found 77 non-crawlable anchors; recon shows many javascript:void(0) links for categories and actions.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace javascript:void(0) navigational anchors with real URLs or semantic buttons.

findings.summary: Public pages expose the indexing signals search engines need: successful HTTP status, canonical URL when appropriate, hreflang for localized variants, robots/sitemap consistency, and no accidental noindex/noarchive policy.
findings.evidence: Homepage/detail return 200 with canonical/sitemap signals, but the public blog index raw fetch returned HTTP 500 while still rendering content.
findings.suggestedFix: Return HTTP 200 for the healthy blog index, or an intentional error page/status when unhealthy.

findings.summary: Served over HTTPS with a sensible Content-Security-Policy and secure, SameSite cookies; no mixed content or obvious transport/header smells.
findings.evidence: HTTPS is used, but CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, and Permissions-Policy are absent; all 15 observed cookies were flagged insecure.
findings.suggestedFix: Add CSP, HSTS, nosniff, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, and secure cookie attributes.

findings.summary: No over-collection of user data, no leaky third parties, and analytics/background data collection is minimised and batched rather than chatty or session-wide by default.
findings.evidence: Load contacted 22 third-party origins and five known trackers; 70 third-party requests transferred 1.33 MB, including Google, Facebook, DoubleClick, Bing, and WebEngage.
findings.suggestedFix: Audit consent and remove/sequence duplicate or low-value trackers after explicit need.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defenses are configured where appropriate: HSTS, clickjacking protection (frame-ancestors / X-Frame-Options), Trusted Types for XSS-sensitive apps, origin isolation, privacy-preserving third-party cookie posture, and sensible Referrer-Policy / Permissions-Policy.
findings.evidence: Only X-Frame-Options was present; HSTS, CSP/frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, and nosniff were absent, and many cookies use SameSite=None without Secure.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy browser defenses in headers and correct SameSite/Secure cookie posture.

findings.summary: HTTP errors, network failures, timeouts and stale data states are handled intentionally: users see useful recovery options rather than blank screens, infinite spinners, broken shells, or misleading success states.
findings.evidence: The blog index returns HTTP 500 while rendering a normal content page, providing a misleading success-like UI and broken status signal rather than intentional recovery.
findings.suggestedFix: Make server status and rendered recovery state agree, with retry/help for failures.

findings.summary: Forms prevent and recover from mistakes humanely: validate after interaction (not prematurely), give clear required-field feedback, announce errors accessibly, and signal invalid fields visibly rather than blaming the user.
findings.evidence: The blank mobile-number submission produced no visible required-field feedback or actionable error.
findings.suggestedFix: Validate after interaction and expose inline plus live-region feedback.

findings.summary: Images and decorative assets are optimised and served at appropriate resolutions; decorative pseudo-element imagery and heavy decorative images are resolution-optimised rather than oversized.
findings.evidence: Of 98 images, 64 use legacy formats, 16 are oversized, 15 lack responsive sources, and 54 lack dimensions.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve responsive AVIF/WebP/SVG assets at display-appropriate sizes with dimensions.

findings.summary: Background work and fetching are not wasteful: background processing is efficient and de-prioritised, and the lightest technique that achieves the result is preferred over heavy or redundant work.
findings.evidence: An idle homepage load executes 50 scripts, transfers 2.12 MB of script, and records 70 third-party requests plus 864.91 ms blocking time.
findings.suggestedFix: Deprioritize background analytics and remove redundant scripts/fetches.

findings.summary: Third-party scripts, fonts, video, audio, animation and heavy media are proportionate to the user value they provide; autoplay or background media is avoided unless essential and resource use is cached or deferred where possible.
findings.evidence: Third parties account for 1.33 MB across 70 requests; duplicate Google tags and Facebook/WebEngage code consume substantial budget before user interaction.
findings.suggestedFix: Set and enforce a third-party byte/request budget and load optional vendors after consent.

findings.summary: Honours prefers-color-scheme: a usable dark mode exists and is driven by the user's preference (color-scheme / prefers-color-scheme / light-dark()), not hard-coded light only.
findings.evidence: The dark-condition screenshot is visually identical to light; computed color-scheme is normal and CSS probe found no dark preference rule.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme: light dark and theme surfaces with prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: Overlays and rich controls use the right primitive: popover (with declarative light-dismiss) for transient UI, dialog for modal flows, details for disclosure, native-but-branded selects and pickers, rather than ad-hoc divs.
findings.evidence: The persistent notification UI is custom chrome rather than a native dialog/popover flow; the DOM reports a role=dialog surface and no popover primitive.
findings.suggestedFix: Use dialog/popover semantics with declarative light-dismiss and focus management.

findings.summary: Minimise non-content chrome and borders so the content is the focus, not the application frame; expressive/decorative visuals serve the content rather than crowd it.
findings.evidence: On mobile, the trial banner, fixed notification prompt, WhatsApp control, header, and app badges crowd the primary preparation content.
findings.suggestedFix: Consolidate promotional chrome and reserve the first viewport for the user’s task.

findings.summary: Layout adapts to narrow viewports with no horizontal overflow and no fixed pixel widths forcing a desktop layout on mobile; viewport meta present; fluid scaling and intrinsic sizing rather than brittle breakpoints.
findings.evidence: The online test-series listing has 8 px horizontal overflow (scrollWidth 368 vs clientWidth 360); other sampled templates did not overflow.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove the listing’s fixed-width overflow and use intrinsic fluid sizing.

findings.summary: Valid doctype and charset, images sized with correct aspect ratio, no deprecated APIs misused, and CSS/HTML are well structured and not needlessly repetitive. (HTTPS, CSP and permission hygiene are judged under be-private-and-secure, not here.)
findings.evidence: Doctype and UTF-8 are valid, but Lighthouse found four aspect-ratio failures and image inspection found 54 images without explicit dimensions.
findings.suggestedFix: Correct image aspect ratios and supply intrinsic width/height.

findings.summary: Permission prompts are requested in context (not on load), and authentication uses modern, phishing-resistant methods (passkeys / WebAuthn) where relevant rather than passwords alone.
findings.evidence: Signup uses a mobile-number/OTP entry with no visible passkey/WebAuthn option; phishing-resistant authentication was not offered on the sampled auth path.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer passkeys/WebAuthn alongside the OTP path and keep prompts user-initiated.

findings.summary: Where the site is an app, it is installable (web app manifest) and offers an offline fallback and works on flaky networks. (Contextual: a brochure or intrinsically-online site may reasonably not need this.)
findings.evidence: No manifest link was present in recon and no offline fallback was evidenced for this app-like exam-preparation service.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a manifest and service-worker offline fallback for core preparation content.

findings.summary: Correct lang and dir attributes, logical CSS properties (inline/block) rather than physical left/right, and translation-ready markup so the layout and reading order survive other languages and writing modes.
findings.evidence: html lang=en is present, but no dir and no logical inline/block properties were detected despite the site exposing language switching and localized content.
findings.suggestedFix: Set direction deliberately and migrate layout spacing/positioning to logical properties.

findings.summary: Input is assisted, not obstructed: correct autocomplete tokens so address, payment, sign-in and sign-up fields autofill, and inputs are highlighted/sized to help the user rather than trip them up.
findings.evidence: The mobile-number step is not represented by a semantic form in the rendered DOM and its input exposes no autocomplete token, reducing autofill/input assistance.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a semantic form, tel input, and autocomplete=tel.

findings.summary: State and route changes use View Transitions (including same-document, cross-document and scroll-driven/staggered) rather than instant, jarring swaps.
findings.evidence: No View Transition CSS/API use was found across the Angular homepage and representative navigation surfaces; state changes are abrupt.
findings.suggestedFix: Progressively enhance meaningful route/state changes with View Transitions and a no-motion fallback.

findings.summary: Tooltips, popovers and menus use CSS anchor positioning (with fallback positions) so they stay attached and reposition correctly rather than being manually positioned.
findings.evidence: The site has dropdown/menu and floating notification UI, but no CSS anchor positioning or fallback-position rules were found.
findings.suggestedFix: Use CSS anchor positioning with position-try fallbacks for attached menus and overlays.

findings.summary: Components adapt to their container with container queries (incl. anchored container queries) and content/state-based styling where reused at different sizes, not only global viewport breakpoints.
findings.evidence: The CSS probe found no container queries; reusable cards/navigation rely on viewport-wide treatment and the listing overflows at 360 px.
findings.suggestedFix: Make reused cards and navigation container-responsive rather than viewport-only.
